The PR's only failed check is the CRAP ratchet: **0 regressions, 11 new functions over threshold 8** (run 42836162956, full log in `ci_failures_full.log`):

```

NEW > 8  js/mergeTrigger.js::runStateMachine: 11
NEW > 8  js/retryMergeGithubPR.js::squashAndFinalize: 10.5
NEW > 8  js/sm/mergeBot.js::mergeApprovedHead: 13
NEW > 8  js/unit-tests/test_postMergeSweep.js::pr1410Provider: 10
NEW > 8  js/unit-tests/test_retryMergeGithubPR.js::laneGlobals: 14
```

`runSweep` (CRAP 16.1, the worst) is the merge-sweep core; `mergeApprovedHead` (13) grew because every exit now renders an `emitDecision` call. Suggested decomposition direction (keep behavior byte-identical — the emission suites pin it):

- `postMergeSweep.runSweep`: extract the provider-primitive gate, the comments-read/ledger phase, and the digest dedup/post tail into helpers (the module already has `resolveMachineThreads` as the model).
- `mergeBot.mergeApprovedHead` / `mergeTrigger.runStateMachine` / `retryMergeGithubPR.squashAndFinalize`: extract the shared `held-decision` render (`emitDecision` + reason string) per exit into a small local helper; the three funnels repeat the same 6–8-line block at each exit.
- Test helpers `pr1410Provider` and `laneGlobals`: split the fixture factories (thread rows vs lane globals vs provider recorder).

Note the ratchet is monotone: once this lands with CRAP ≤ 8 for the new functions, the baseline absorbs them. Unit tests are green (9497 passed in CI; I reproduced locally), so this is purely complexity/coverage debt on the new code.

comments.body:
⚠️ severity: IMPORTANT —
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the sweep can never reach PR #1410 itself — the ticket's live test case has no trigger**

`mergedThreadSweep` rides the merged-PR close tick (`decideClosedPrActions`), which only ever runs for issues listed by `listMachineIssues` — and that search filters `is:issue is:open` (`js/common/smProvider.js:647-655`). A closed issue is terminal: no later SM tick ever revisits the PR.

That is exactly gh-1410's state per this PR's own root-cause note ("PR merged, issue closed, thread open, nobody scheduled anything"). So after this ships:

- **Future** merged-with-residue PRs → swept on their close tick ✓
- **PR #1410 itself** → its issue is already closed, `is:open` excludes it, the sweep never fires, and its open IMPORTANT thread stays unresolved forever — the precise debt this issue was opened to recover.

ticket.md (Design c) states the live acceptance: *"Test case: PR #1410's thread must be picked up by the sweep on its next run after this ships."* AC3's scripted-payload variant is satisfied (the test passes), but the live variant cannot pass without an explicit recovery step. Please add one of:

1. reopen gh-1410's linked issue before/at merge so the next tick plans `[mergedThreadSweep, closeIssue]` for it, or
2. a one-shot backfill (a dry run of `postMergeSweep.runSweep` against PR #1410 via a scratch job), or
3. record on the issue that the live case is superseded by the scripted-payload AC3 test and why.

If gh-1410's issue is in fact still open, this finding dissolves — but then please say so on the thread, because the root-cause narrative in the PR description asserts the close path already closed it.

comments.author: unknown
comments.body:
💡 severity: SUGGESTION —
💡 **SUGGESTION: the marker sentence overstates "auto-resolved" for the machine bucket**

At `mergeNote.js:123-127` the human-readable half of the marker renders:

```
🧵 Merged with residue (gh-1420): 3 review thread(s) were open at merge time —
2 machine-owned (auto-resolved by the merge backstop, findings ride the
review debt ledger / digest issue), 1 human (left open per gh-744).
```

But `residueCountsOf` computes `machine = counted + ackThreads + holdThreads`, where `counted` threads are **defered to the digest** (not auto-resolved) and `holdThreads` are expired human-hour holds. Only `autoResolved = resolved + ackResolved` were actually auto-resolved. So a merge with 2 counted + 0 resolved says "2 machine-owned (auto-resolved...)" — wrong for the counted bucket.

The JSON payload is the protocol and it is correct; only the sentence misleads a human reader auditing "what actually happened to my threads". Cheap fix while the crap rework touches this file anyway:

```js
var note = '\uD83E\uDD9A Merged with residue (gh-1420): ' +
    residue.openThreadsAtMerge + ' review thread(s) were open at merge time — ' +
    residue.machine + ' machine-owned (' + residue.autoResolved + ' auto-resolved; the rest' +
    ' deferred to the review debt ledger / digest issue), ' + residue.human +
    ' human (left open per gh-744).';
```

(or simply drop the "(auto-resolved …)" parenthetical — the payload and the ledger marker already say it precisely).

**Summary**: The design is sound and the root-cause analysis is real — but CI is red: the `crap` ratchet fails at 65879cee with **11 new functions over threshold 8** (`runSweep` 16.1, `mergeApprovedHead` 13, `laneGlobals` 14, …), which is 🚨 BLOCKING per policy. Two IMPORTANT items: the sweep's only trigger (the merged-PR close tick on `is:open` issues) can never reach PR #1410 itself, whose issue is already closed per the PR's own root cause — the ticket's live test case needs an explicit recovery path; and AC4's root-cause note is on the PR description only, not on the issue this PR closes.

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 crap gate red — decompose the 11 over-threshold functions (full list in comment 1); unit tests are green (9497 passed in CI, reproduced locally), so this is pure complexity debt
- ⚠️ sweep reachability — gh-1410's closed issue is invisible to `listMachineIssues` (`is:open`), so the live pickup promised in ticket Design c needs a reopen/backfill (comment 2)
- ⚠️ AC4 — paste the root-cause note onto issue #1420 before merge (comment 3)
- 💡 marker sentence says "auto-resolved" for defered/hold threads — payload is correct, prose overstates (comment 4)

**Digest** (advisory, no threads):
- `js/common/postMergeSweep.js:106` — `severityClassOfThread` duplicates `mergeBackstop`'s private helper verbatim; export & delegate when the crap rework touches these files (duplication gate passed)
- `js/retryMergeGithubPR.js:364` — held line renders `machineThreads=0 humanThreads=0` on a *thrown* gate fault (unknown ≠ 0); the `allowlist=0` grep audit could misread it — consider `?` for the fault case
- `js/common/mergeNote.js:295` — the `::warning::` reason interpolates raw exception text; a multi-line message would break the one-line annotation shape (low risk)
- `js/unit-tests/test_mergeNote.js:136` — stray `human2: undefined` fixture key in `residueBackstop()`

**Next Steps**:
1. Fix the CRAP ratchet (extract helpers in the 11 flagged functions — tests already pin behavior, refactor is safe)
2. Resolve the PR #1410 recovery path (reopen its issue or add a one-shot backfill) and confirm AC4's note is on the issue
3. Re-push; the emission/dedup test coverage is otherwise strong and should keep passing unchanged
